affectedPublicSurfaces: every authenticated /v1/* route's auth dependency (get_current_user) — behaviour changes for one previously-failing case: a validly-signed Supabase JWT whose sub has no public.users row
GET /v1/shops, the first route a newly signed-in seller reaches from the connect-shop screen

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: the API candidate unit on its idle blue/green port, before the nginx upstream cutover

journeys.name: first-time-identity-is-provisioned-once
journeys.entryUrl: GET /v1/shops on the candidate port, bearer = a validly-signed JWT for a sub with no users row
assertions: 200 with an empty list, not 401 'User not found'
exactly one public.users row exists for that sub afterwards
a second identical request creates no further row

journeys.name: an-unverified-token-provisions-nothing
journeys.entryUrl: GET /v1/shops on the candidate port with a malformed, expired, and wrongly-signed token
assertions: the response detail is the generic 'Invalid or expired credentials' and never echoes the parser's reason (ADR-061 / #902)
the public.users row count is unchanged

htmlRoutes: not-applicable: backend auth dependency, no HTML route

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration. This writes a row through the existing model. Rows provisioned by the candidate are readable by the stable release, and vice versa.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: roll back to the retained previous release; already-provisioned rows stay valid and orphan nothing, and new identities simply return to 401

acceptanceCommands: ruff check backend tests scripts && mypy backend/src/juli_backend --ignore-missing-imports --disable-error-code=valid-type
doNotInfer: Do NOT verify this through the shared `session` fixture. It is SQLite even when DATABASE_URL names Postgres — a DB-level claim made through it is untested. `users` is policy-gated, so build a real engine the way tests/integration/test_series_source_enforced.py does.
Do NOT provision before verify_supabase_jwt succeeds. A malformed or unsigned token must create no row and still 401.
Do NOT echo the JWT parser's reason in the 401 detail — ADR-061 / #902 require the generic message.
Do NOT write a second provisioning path. UsersRepo.get_or_create already exists and is used by four services/tiktok/* stores; reuse it.
Do NOT grant the provisioned user a shop, a capability, or a credential. Zero shops is the correct, honest state and the connect-shop screen already renders it.
Do NOT treat the concurrency case as theoretical — two first requests for the same sub must yield exactly one row, with the loser's IntegrityError handled rather than surfaced.
Do NOT bind the sandbox shop to the new user in code. That is a one-off owner DB act after this lands, not a migration and not part of this slice.
